english.title: Display any writing / sign / visible representation with intent to cause harassment / alarm or distress based on sex
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), because of the sex or presumed sex of **(..SPECIFY PERSON..), and with intent to cause that person harassment, alarm or distress displayed writing, a sign or other visible representation, namely **(..SPECIFY THING DISPLAYED..), which was threatening, abusive or insulting thereby causing that person or another harassment, alarm or distress
english.legislation: Contrary to section 4B(1) and (4) of the Public Order Act 1986.

english.notes:
(i) Where the specific date of the offence is not known, the charge should read: "...on a date between X and Y...". where 'X' is the last date before the first date on which the offence could have occurred, and 'Y' is the first date after the last date it could have occurred.
(e.g. a factory closes Friday evening to Monday morning. It is broken into over the weekend. The charge should read: "...on a date between X (Thursday's date) and Y (Tuesday's date)...".)
(ii) Practical Considerations:
(a) 'Threatening' includes verbal and physical threats and violent conduct
'Abusive' means degrading or reviling language
'Insulting' means scornful, insolent, contemptuous
(b) There must be evidence that the suspect actually intended to cause harassment, alarm or distress, not merely that that was the consequence of his behaviour.
(c) There must be evidence that harassment, alarm or distress was actually caused.
(iii) Where there is no evidence that the offence was committed on the basis of sex, consider section 4A of the Public Order Act 1986.
(iv) Where there is repeated harassment of individuals, consider the definition of "harassment" and the offence as provided by sections 1 and 2 sections 1 and 2 respectively of the Protection from Harassment Act 1997.
(vi) See also offence wording: H101433 - relating to the use threatening / abusive / insulting words / behaviour to cause harassment / alarm / distress based on person's sex.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and / or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and / or a fine.
Time limit for prosecutions:
None

The maximum penalty on summary conviction may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 4B(4) of this Act and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2022.
